title: Investigating the K+ sensitivity of cellular metabolism by extracellular flux analysis
protocol: Design the experiment using Seahorse Wave Desktop Software.
Install the software and run the application.
Open a “blank” file under the templates section.
Define the conditions of the experiment in the “definitions” section.
Start with defining injection strategies.
Define assay media and cell type.
Define pretreatments, including treatment with DMSO as control.
Add Gramicidin dissolved in DMSO as an experimental condition.
Include additional pretreatments if necessary.
Define the assay media used as SM-0K+ and SM-140K+ medium.
Cell treatment with gramicidin adjusts the intracellular K+ concentration to match the extracellular [K+] in SM-0K+ (0 mM K+) or SM-140K+ (140.0 mM K+) medium.
Define the cell type used, such as HEK293, HeLa, and INS-1 832/13.
Create a “background” group that cannot be altered or removed.
For each condition, add a new group specifying injection strategy, pretreatments, assay media, and cell type.
Accurately define the groups to ensure sorted results after assay completion and result export.
Assign defined groups to the wells by clicking the group on the left side.
Click the wells comprising the respective groups on the right side.
Use the “distribute groups” button to fairly spread the groups on the plate.
Recommend including at least four blanks on the plate.
Define the protocol used for analyzing the cells.
Measure a baseline without injection if only basal ECAR/OCR ratios are of interest.
Alter the protocol depending on the desired read-out and injections at different time points.
Perform at least 4 measurement cycles.
Save the defined protocol to re-open it when starting the measurement.
Remove the cells from the incubator.
Aspirate the medium and wash twice with 6–10 mL pre-warmed PBS.
Aspirate PBS and add 2 mL of pre-warmed trypsin-EDTA at a concentration of 0.05% in PBS to the cells.
Put the cell dish back into the incubator.
Check for cell detachment after 3 min at 37°C, 5% CO2 using a cell culture microscope.
If cells appear round shaped and detached from the surface of the culture dish, proceed to step 3d.
If cells are still attached, prolong the treatment in trypsin-EDTA/PBS but check every minute for cell detachment.
After detachment, stop the enzymatic reaction immediately by adding at least a five- to six-fold amount of the respective cell culture medium with 10% FCS.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge for 5 min at 200 rcf.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL of cell culture full medium (DMEM + 10% FCS / RPMI 1640 + 10% FCS).
Determine the cell number by using a Bürker-Türk counting chamber or any other method of choice.
Adjust the glass plate to the chamber and fill each of the two chambers with 15 μL of the cell suspension when using a Bürker-Türk counting chamber.
Resuspend cells thoroughly before pipetting them into the chamber.
Count all cells visible in the four large squares on the edges, with each square consisting of 16 smaller squares.
Divide this number by 4 to calculate the average number counted from the top and bottom chamber.
Multiply the number by 10,000 to determine the number of cells per milliliter cell suspension.
Prepare HEK293, HeLa, and INS-1 832/13 cells for seeding according to the previously defined layout.
Dilute HEK293 cells in full medium (DMEM + 10% FCS) to achieve a concentration of 560,000 cells per milliliter.
Seed 70,000 HEK293 cells per well using a final volume of 125 μL per well.
Dilute HeLa cells in full medium (DMEM + 10% FCS) to achieve a concentration of 400,000 cells per milliliter.
Seed 50,000 HeLa cells per well using a final volume of 125 μL per well.
Dilute INS-1 832/13 cells in full medium (RPMI 1640 + 10% FCS) to achieve a concentration of 800,000 cells per milliliter.
Seed 100,000 INS-1 832/13 cells per well using a final volume of 125 μL per well.
Transfer 125 μL of the diluted cell suspension into each well of the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture Microplate, leaving the corner wells blank and not seeding cells into edge wells.
Add 125 μL of full medium (DMEM + 10% FCS) to the 4 edge wells which will serve as blanks during measurement.
Put the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture Microplate in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Cultivate cells for 14–20 hours to allow cell attachment.
Keep wells on the edges of the plate free from cells and add complemented medium instead.
Hydrate the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Remove the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge (green plate) carefully.
Place the 96-well plate so that sensor modules look upwards.
Add 100 μL of calibrant solution into every well of the clear 96-well plate.
Re-insert the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge into the 96-well plate.
Incubate the hydrated Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge in a 37°C incubator without CO2 for 14–20 hours.
Switch on the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer one day before the experiment.
Start the controlling software of the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer.
Pre-warm the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer by allowing it to pre-heat overnight.
Check the display of the device to ensure it is pre-heating.
Transfer 48.725 mL of both Seahorse assay media, SM-0K+ and SM-140K+, into a sterile 50 mL falcon under sterile conditions.
Place the transferred media in a 37°C water bath.
Once the media are warmed, add the desired amounts of D-glucose, L-glutamine, and pyruvate.
Adjust the pH to 7.40 at 37°C.
Add 275 μl of 1.0 M D-glucose to the medium.
Add 500 μl of 100× L-glutamine to the medium.
Add 500 μl of 100× sodium pyruvate to the medium.
Adjust the pH of the complemented media to 7.40 using a magnetic stirrer equipped with a heating unit.
Keep the temperature of the medium at 37°C during pH adjustment.
Adjust the pH of SM-0K+ medium to 7.40 using 0.1 N NaOH dropwise.
Adjust the pH of SM-140K+ medium to 7.40 using 0.1 N KOH dropwise.
Prepare a 15 mM gramicidin stock solution in DMSO.
Add 3.33 μL of 15 mM gramicidin stock solution to each vial containing SM-0K+ and SM-140K+ medium, yielding a final concentration of 5 μM.
Transfer 2×10 mL of SM-0K+ medium into 15 mL tubes.
Transfer 2×10 mL of SM-140K+ medium into 15 mL tubes.
Add equivalent amounts of DMSO to the SM-0K+ and SM-140K+ media.
If a 15 mM gramicidin stock was used, add 3.33 μL of DMSO to each vial containing SM-0K+ and SM-140K+ medium.
Keep all media at a temperature of 37°C using a water bath until usage.
Adjust the pH to 7.40 for both SM-0K+ and SM-140K+ media carefully and slowly.
Take care to adjust the pH at 37°C as the assay is performed at this temperature.
Optional: Keep the medium free from D-glucose and inject glucose via the ports of the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge.
Load the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge into the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer.
Run the experiment using Seahorse Wave Desktop Software on the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer.
Insert the hydrated sensor cartridge onto the utility plate after removing its lid.
Place the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge into the device with well A1 at the rear position on the left-back.
Confirm the insertion of the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge.
Remove the lid from the Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge before inserting it into the device to avoid damage and ensure results.
Exchange medium in half of the plate for SM-0K+ medium to remove residual K+.
Adjust [K+] by exchanging medium in the other half of the plate with SM-140K+ medium.
Prepare the cells for the extracellular flux analysis assay.
Remove the cells from the incubator and check the wells for cell confluency.
Exchange medium twice with SM-0K+ or SM-140K+ buffer if cells show a confluency of ∼90%.
Remove the culture medium from the cells, leaving 25 μL remaining in the wells.
Add 125 μL of the respective assay medium (SM-0K+, SM-140K+, both without DMSO or gramicidin).
Remove 150 μL from the wells and add 150 μL of the respective assay medium (SM-0K+, SM-140K+).
Treat half of the wells washed with SM-0K+ medium with SM-0K+ + DMSO or SM-0K+ + gramicidin.
Treat half of the wells washed with SM-140K+ medium with SM-140K+ + DMSO or SM-140K+ + gramicidin.
Check the wells for the presence and attachment of cells using a microscope.
Place the cells in a 37°C incubator without CO2 for 20 min.
Remove the plate from the incubator after 20 min of incubation.
Replace SM-0K+ and SM-140K+ medium containing DMSO / gramicidin with respective assay medium without DMSO and gramicidin.
Carefully remove all 150 μL from the plate without disturbing or scraping the cells.
Replace removed solution with 150 μL of SM-0K+ or SM-140K+ free from DMSO, respectively.
Incubate the cells at 37°C without CO2 for 10 min.
Incubation times of cells should not be shortened.
Put the plate into the device immediately after respective incubation times.
Avoid spill over from different wells during repetitive handling of plates.
Finish the assay by following steps on the screen of the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer.
Confirm to finish the assay once complete.
The Seahorse XF96 Sensor Cartridge will move out of the device on top of the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture plate.
Both plates can be discarded after finishing the assay.
Do not discard the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture plate if normalization for protein concentration or other parameters is required.
Normalize OCR and ECAR values based on the method chosen.
Open the data from the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer in the Seahorse Wave Desktop software.
Select “normalize” in the top bar within the software.
Enter the seeded cell number / 103 for each well in the table and confirm the normalization by selecting “apply”.
Carefully remove the supernatants of the cells without disturbing the cells at the bottom.
We recommend removing the medium by pipetting.
Air-dry the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture Plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for at least 1 h to remove any residual medium.
Freeze the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture Plate over-night at -80°C.
Thaw the Seahorse XF96 Cell Culture Plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for at least 1 hour.
Return the plate to the -80°C freezer for at least 2 hours and repeat the freeze-thaw cycle two more times.
Mix 50 parts of BCA reagent A with 1 part of BCA reagent B to prepare the working reagent (WR).
Prepare enough WR for 96 protein determinations by mixing 3 mL of BCA reagent A with 60 μL of BCA reagent B.
Add 50 μL of ddH2O to each well except wells A12 and H12 to solubilize the cell fragments.
Put 5 μL of a 2 mg/mL BSA stock solution in well A12, then add 45 μL of ddH2O for a protein amount of 10 μg per well.
Add 50 μL of a 2 mg/mL BSA stock solution to well H12 for a protein amount of 100 μg per well.
After all wells are pre-filled with 50 μL of solution, add 30 μL of the WR per well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C without CO2 for 30 minutes.
Incubate for 30 minutes.
Read absorbance at 562 nm.
Calculate the protein concentration per well.
Subtract the average of wells A1 and H1 from every other well.
Generate a calibration curve using BSA standards by plotting blank corrected absorbance values against protein concentrations.
Use Microsoft Excel to generate a linear function through the plotted points.
Solve the equation for x to calculate the protein concentration for each well.
Open data from the Seahorse XF96 Analyzer in the Seahorse Wave Desktop software.
Select “normalize” in the top bar within the software.
Enter calculated protein concentrations in μg for each well in the table.
Confirm normalization by selecting “apply”.
The software will display normalized OCR and ECAR values over-time.
Analyze the normalized data using a program of choice.
Export the data to Microsoft Excel.
Take the average of several time-points that were measured without injection for each well.
Divide the averaged ECARs by the averaged OCRs for each well.
Average the ECAR/OCRs for SM-0K+ medium of each cell line treated with DMSO or gramicidin.
Divide each value of SM-140K+ medium by the averaged value obtained from step 1 for the corresponding condition (DMSO/gramicidin).
Compare the resulting values to determine the effect of high K+ on ECAR/OCR ratio.
